$comment: Authored from docs/plan/meet-v5-design.md (§3.2.4, §4.2, §8.4) before any of it is built: M0-PR1 publishes it so the M1 backend, the app and the tests share one table. The status is a text CHECK on public.meet_matches, not an enum, so contracts/v1/enums.json never lists it and contracts/tools/generate_v1.py does not cross-check this file (its literal-pair check reads job.json only). M1-PR5 implements it; if the SQL disagrees, this file changes in the same PR.
subject: public.meet_matches.status
note: A match is a pair, stored low/high (CHECK profile_low < profile_high), between two opaque meet_profiles ids. A client never assigns a status: it calls a verb and reads the result. Every client sees profile ids only, never auth uids (ADR-0026 D15). Erasing a Meet profile deletes its matches by ON DELETE CASCADE, which is not a transition.

actors.S: system: a cron sweep or a server-side side effect
actors.A: admin, meet_moderator or super_admin in country scope

states.name: pending
states.meaning: Matched, nobody has written yet. The 24-hour timer is running

states.name: active
states.meaning: Engaged: the first message has been delivered. No timer

states.name: expired
states.meaning: The timer ran out before either member wrote

states.name: unmatched
states.meaning: A member unmatched. The pair is never shown to each other again

states.name: closed_block
states.meaning: A member blocked the other. Never restored, even after an unblock

states.name: closed_moderation
states.meaning: Closed by a moderation decision about either member

transitions.guard: A like (or super interest) on a profile that already liked the caller; the target is in the caller's daily set or nearby list, a revealed liker or a super-interest sender; neither has blocked the other; no live match exists for the pair. The pair advisory lock serialises simultaneous mutual likes
effects: the pair's conversation is opened, or reopened if one exists (one per pair)
both are notified with meet_match, deep link /meet/matches/<id>
the swipe result returns {matched: true, match_id, conversation_id, expires_at}

transitions.guard: The recipient accepts a pending reach request
effects: the recipient's profile is unlocked for the sender
transitions.open: Authored as pending so every new match carries the same 24-hour rule. M2-PR8 confirms or changes this when it builds reach requests

transitions.guard: The first message of either member is delivered. A send the contact filter blocks is not delivered and does not engage the match
expires_at has passed with engaged_at still NULL (the meet-sweeps job, every 5 minutes)
The caller is a member of the match
effects: both swipes get pass_until = 'infinity', so neither is shown the other again

transitions.guard: Either member blocks the other, directly or through meet_report with p_block (the default)
effects: public.blocks row with source 'meet', which applies to errands too (OD-52)
the conversation and its open game rounds close, and each stops seeing the other's statuses
M2: pending reach requests between the pair close
the blocked member is never told

transitions.guard: A moderation decision removes either member from Meet: a suspension or ban (admin_meet_suspend, admin_meet_approve_ban), or the profile set to 'removed'
effects: nothing tells the other member why
transitions.open: Which decisions close matches, and whether a lifted suspension leaves them closed, is settled in M1-PR4. A discovery hold (D16) is reversible and is not one of them

invariants: At most one live match per pair: a partial UNIQUE (profile_low, profile_high) WHERE status IN ('pending','active'), plus the pair advisory lock in meet_swipe, so two simultaneous mutual likes produce exactly one match and one meet_match notification each.
Only pending expires. An active match has no timer.
A block wins from any live state, and an unblock never restores a match or reopens its conversation.
Closed states are terminal. A later match between the same pair is a new row with a new id; the conversation row is reused because there is one per pair.
Every read re-checks blocks, holds and suspensions: a closed or hidden counterpart reads as ERR_MEET_MATCH_NOT_FOUND or ERR_MEET_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND, never as a reason.
No presence: a match never shows whether the other person is online (ADR-0026 D20).

timeouts.on_expiry: one meet_reminder notification to both members, reminded_at set; no transition

errors_a_client_will_see.ERR_MEET_MATCH_NOT_FOUND: meet_unmatch on a match the caller is not in, or one already closed or hidden. Indistinguishable on purpose.
errors_a_client_will_see.ERR_MEET_CONVERSATION_CLOSED: Sending into the conversation of an expired, unmatched or closed match.
errors_a_client_will_see.ERR_MEET_DAILY_LIMIT: meet_swipe over the day's like or super-interest allowance.
